## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">How do we quantify academic impact using test data
• The pandemic was like a “headwind” that (presumably) slowed down the learning of
students due to a variety of factors.
• We can use test data in two ways to quantify the impact of this headwind:
• Best way: Quantify how much the rate of learning (i.e., growth) slowed:
• ILEARN: Use historical skip-year growth norms to quantify growth and compare to pre-COVID growth.
• ACCESS: Use historical consecutive-year growth norms and compare to pre-COVID growth
• NWEA-MAP: Provides growth data based upon historical norms but we currently don’t have historical
growth to compare to.
• Next best way: Look at how much 2021 status changed:
• ILEARN: Use 2019 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
• ACCESS: Use 2020 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
• Adjustments include (potentially) imputation for missing data as well as propensity score matching for
• NOTE: When providing 2021 data, users will (correctly) want to compare their data to
2019 (or 2020 with ACCESS). The task is to make sure that such a comparison is an
apples-to-apples comparison.
Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 2</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">How do we quantify academic impact using test data
• Historical consecutive and skip-year growth norms were created for ILEARN and
ACCESS in May, 2021 for use with 2021 ILEARN and ACCESS data.
• We can use test data in two ways to quantify the impact of this headwind:
• Best way: Quantify how much the rate of learning (i.e., growth) slowed:
• ILEARN: Use historical skip-year growth norms to quantify growth and compare to pre-COVID growth.
• ACCESS: Use historical consecutive-year growth norms and compare to pre-COVID growth
• NWEA-MAP: Provides growth data based upon historical norms but we currently don’t have historical
growth to compare to.
• Next best way: Look at how much 2021 status changed:
• ILEARN: Use 2019 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
• ACCESS: Use 2020 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
• Adjustments include (potentially) imputation for missing data as well as propensity score matching for
• NOTE: When providing 2021 data, users will (correctly) want to compare their data to
2019 (or 2020 with ACCESS). The task is to make sure that such a comparison is an
apples-to-apples comparison.
Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 3</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Results
• As the Board of Education presentation indicated, overall academic impact was
moderate/large in ELA and large in mathematics.
• Both status-based analyses as well as growth-based analyses support these
findings.
• The following tables illustrate numerically what these impacts were.
• For rough comparison, the effect size impacts we are seeing for achievement
are roughly 1 to 5 times as large as what was reported for Hurricane Katrina in
Louisiana depending upon grade and content area. (Effect sizes of -0.06 and
-0.17 are associated with Katrina).
• Groups experiencing minimal impact should be scrutinized closely with regard
to pre-pandemic level of educational efficacy.
Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 4</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/15.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Performance by initial level of achievement
• A consistent finding put forward from interim assessment reports and
picked up by educational pundits is that it is the most ”vulnerable”
who are experiencing the biggest impacts.
• Based solely upon demographic subgroup analysis, that finding was
not supported.
• To dig deeper we regularly look at SGP distributions by prior score
decile. For cohort referenced SGPs we expect a uniform distribution.
For baseline referenced SGPs, deviations from uniform indicate
impact.

Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 15</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/16.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">School level impact
• We are currently in the process of finalizing school level impact
analyses and want to share some of the initial looks at these results.
• To calculate impact at the school level we calculate for each school:
Unadjusted Impact = Median SGP2019- Median SGP2021
• We adjust for regression to the mean for this difference score by using
pre-pandemic (2017 to 2019) school level median SGP scores.
• The following bubble plots illustrate academic impact for Indiana
Schools.

Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 16</div>
```
